Features include difficulty settings, level passcodes (in a Simon Says fashion), health bar, destroyable background elements, many different powerups with a limited timeout, and numerous bonuses. Multiple versions exist with different music.

198948.overview:
Published in ANALOG Magazine Issue 62 - 07/88

Analog Man is similar to BurgerTime, the player has to go over platforms which will fall down on utter platforms, which however will fall down on other utter platforms.

Those platforms can stun enemies for a few seconds.

198949.overview: Androton is a collect'em game, in which you have to collect various treasures, while avoiding hostile androids, called Androtons. From A.N.A.L.O.G. magazine issue 25.

199069.overview: Published in the June 1983 issue of Compute! magazine, in it you guide your spaceship, carrying emergency medical supplies, through a dangerous asteroid storm. A great deal depends on your skills as a navigator. Many times the success or failure of your mission will depend on your ability to make split-second decisions under pressure.

199101.overview: Amazing is a maze collect 'em up game for the Atari 8-bit line of computers. It was developed by David N. Plotkin and published in May 1985 issue of Antic Magazine.

199103.overview: Alien Asylums (also known as Alien Asylum) is an arcade collect 'em up for the Atari 8-bit computers. It was developed by Spencer Craske and published by Antic Software in the 85/10 issue of Antic Magazine.

199178.overview: A computerized version of Yahtzee developed by Clayton Walnum and published as a type-in listing in the 05/86 issue of Analog Magazine.

199189.overview: A-Rogue (or Atari Rogue) is a BASIC interpretation of the famous RPG that spawned the "Roguelike" genre. This was developed by Robert Jung and published as a type-in listing in Vol. 6 / No. 1 of Antic Magazine in 1987. This was the first time that Rogue got an implementation on the Atari 8-bit computers. An official port of Rogue was released a year later by Mastertronic, but only in Europe.

199200.overview:
A game in which you have to avoid asteroids for as long as you can to rack up points.

Written by Cliff McConnell and published by Virgin Books as a type-in listing in the book "Games for Your Atari 600XL" in 1984.

199247.overview: Air Raid 2000 is a game in which you have to shoot down enemies and rescue hostages. It plays like sort of a cross's between Defender and Choplifter. The game was developed by Erik Warpaw, and released in the 83/11 issue of Antic Magazine.

199248.overview: Alpha Run is a race, or chase, run over letters or numbers in sequence without exploding the bombs that also lie in the way. A simple game, it teaches the alphabet order and the number sequence 1 through 9. The little blue race car is controlled by a joystick in port One. When the car runs over a number or a letter in proper sequence, the number or letter disappears. If the car runs over a bomb, hits a wall, or touches a number out of sequence, everything explodes and the game starts over. If the sequence is completed, the bombs are rendered harmless. Run over them to end the game. Your final score equals the time elapsed during the run.

199337.overview:
Asteroid Miners is a space-themed arcade game for the 8-bit Atari.

Your home planet is in dire need of specific resources, which can only be found in an asteroid field in a dangerous realm of space. The player controls a large mining vessel, and has a limited time span to scoop up the valuable gold and blue asteroids, while avoiding the unstable and worthless white asteroids. If the player scoops up all asteroids with time remaining, they enter a bonus round on a secondary field, where they try to gather additional resources for bonus points. There are 3 difficulty levels. On level 1, asteroids are stable, and time is plentiful. On the higher levels, new asteroids appear during gameplay, and can damage the mining vessel. Furthermore, white asteroids might explode on impact with the miner.

199483.overview: An educational maze game developed by Jeffrey Stanton and published in the book Atari Graphics and Arcade Game Design in 1984.

199484.overview:
You awaken with a headache and total amnesia.  You don't know where you are or even what your name is.  And what is this strange power you now possess?  Every time you use it, you hear a loud noise!  You would like to move around and find out more, but there's a small problem.  Monsters are everywhere and they're trying to kill you!  Welcome to Adventure Island . . .

This game combines elements of fantasy role-playing and text adventures.  Discovering your identity is a mystery you must solve.  Meanwhile, you're a fighter seeking treasure, exploring caves, and doing battle with multitudes of monsters.

Adventure Island is a text adventure-RPG developed by Robert Lee and published as a seven-page BASIC type-in program in Antic Magazine, volume 3, issue 7, dated November 1984.

199489.overview: A text adventure game design system from CodeWriter Corporation in 1984.

199514.overview: Not to be confused with the Atari 2600 classic, this is a standard old school computer text adventure published by Creative Computing Software in 1980.

199684.overview:
Action Adventures is a set of three compiled BASIC games: 


• Climber-Scale the massive skyscraper! Bricks are falling over the top floor of the skyscraper onto the people below! Only you can scale the outside of the building to stop the dangerous bricks!

• G*Man The angry G*Men are on your trail! You have to get rid of all the damaging evidence before they can catch you! You must clean up the city and clean up your act!

• Diamond Dig - Your spacecraft is almost out of precious fuel. The only nearby planet is a small asteroid full of large diamonds. You must land there and dig up the diamonds to convert into the needed fuel! Dig it?

199685.overview:
A.D. 2044: Seksmisja is a graphical point and click adventure game based in plot on the Polish film Seksmisja. The player is a male imprisoned in a world populated only by women. The goal of the game is to escape, and restore the place of males in the world. 

The interface is joystick driven, commands are issued by using the button and then selecting from available pop up options, or clicking on some commands always available like movement.

199686.overview:
Alfa-Boot is a Polish language adventure game with a point-and-click interface; the protagonist is a special agent, sent out to stop a radioactive leak in a nuclear submarine down in the ocean.

The game uses a simple interface where the player can move a cursor around to select an object in the first-person-view image of the location he's in, and interact with this object in a number of ways. Many objects can be examined, with their descriptions appearing at the bottom of the screen. There is also an ever-present "go" option which allows the player to follow any exit out of the room, including those not visible on screen.

199692.overview:
Android Attack is a simple Berzerk clone which bears no resemblance to similarly named games for other 8-bit computers. 

Advertising copy reads: 
The nuclear reactor in our top-secret installation has malfunctioned and is in danger of melting down! You've been chosen to go in and manually release the cooling water. Now only one problem remains - there isn't time to deactive the Security Androids guarding the unmanned installation, so you'll have to fight your way in, release the water, then escape before the entire underground laboratory fills with water! If you survive this mission, we've got another for you, only this time there are more levels to get through and the Androids are meaner!

199697.overview:
Assault Force is a 3D game similar to Battlezone. The player navigates an attack vehicle blowing up aliens and looking for fuel. Ground and air alien units attack the player. 

The original Atari version came with a special "Super Charger Power Booster" cartridge which has a math coprocessor used while running to achieve the 3D graphics. The game was later cracked and modified to not need the additional hardware.

199892.overview: Akin to Ali Baba and Ultima, this game offers you the roleplaying global challenge filled with adventure, danger and dozens of friends and foes, from cardinals to cannibals, asps to tigers. ATW is unparalleled in scope, with 40 endless scrolling regions - from London through the African jungles and the Orient to New York. ATW has game saves and high score Hall of Fame. No two games are ever the same. For a price much less than other graphic adventures, you can embark on your own global odyssey.

199901.overview: A WW2 strategy game for 1 or 2 players based on the aftermath of the Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor.

200401.overview: Draw astrological charts based on birth date and birthplace. The Astrology program computes the location of the sun, moon and planets at the time of a person's birth and displays the result on a horoscope using finely detailed graphics. A chart of the aspects of the sun, moon and planets also displays. Keplerian elements are used to compute the various positions to an accuracy of one to two degrees for any time this century.

200445.overview:
You're the sole crew member aboard the Advent X-5, a space ship designed to transport small animals.  Your most recent mission was to take some animals to a planet called Klybex-6 to test their reactions to its thick atmosphere and low gravity.  But on the way to Klybex-6, a meteor storm forced you to crash-land the Advent X-5 on Klybez-7.

You're now stranded on the ship, and must get to the emergency shuttle craft and blast off to the nearest star base . . .

Advent X-5 is a text adventure developed by J.D. Casten and published as a four-page type-in BASIC program in Antic Magazine, volume 3, issue 7, dated November 1984.

200712.overview:
Acrobat is a game developed by Peter Rizzuto and it was from volume 7, issue 2 of Compute! dated February 1985.

The game is simple. Run and jump over objects and rack up points until you die. Quite possibly one of the earliest examples of an endless runner game.

There is also another guy that throws arrows at you that you have to jump over as well.

206115.overview: Guide your balloon through the caves in this German game heavily inspired by Crazy Balloon. Developed by KE-Soft and published in the September 1989 issue of Zong magazine.

209365.overview: Compilation release of Adventureland, Pirate Adventure, and Mission Impossible. The games are controlled through the use of written commands. These can consist of a single word, such as those used for player character movement, including north, south, east, west, up, and down. They can also take the form of simple, two-word verb/noun phrases, such as "climb tree". Although the game can recognize about 120 words, the parser only takes the first three letters into account. This means not only that the parser occasionally misidentifies words, but also that commands can be truncated: "lig lam" would be interpreted as "light lamp."

209368.overview: Compilation of Voodoo Castle, The Count, and Strange Odyssey. The games are text adventures, controlled through the use of written commands. These can consist of a single word, such as those used for player character movement, including north, south, east, west, up, and down. They can also take the form of simple, two-word verb/noun phrases, such as "climb tree". Although the game can recognize about 120 words, the parser only takes the first three letters into account. This means not only that the parser occasionally misidentifies words, but also that commands can be truncated: "lig lam" would be interpreted as "light lamp."

209371.overview: A simple card game in which two cards are drawn the player bets on whether the next card will be mathematically in the range between the two existing cards or not.

209434.overview: Alien Attack is a simplistic Space Invaders style game - alien ships appear on the top half of the screen, and you must maneuver side to side with your ship at the bottom, firing vertically to hit them. The alien ships start out very wide and each successive shot makes them shrink horizontally, making them harder to hit.

209449.overview: A compilation release of Spy's Demise, The Spy Strikes Back, and Thunderbombs. Spy's Demise is a vaguely Pac-Man style game, where you gather intelligence in various floors of a building while avoiding guards. The Spy Strikes Back repeats the theme of avoiding guards while maneuvering through 5 different maps. Thunderbombs is an arcade shooter with enemies on multiple sides of the screen.

209450.overview: Compilation of three games, Ribbit! (which is a re-labeled Froggie from Ed Fries, used without his permission), Rescue Sub, and Bug Out. Keypunch as a publisher used repackaged or relabeled software on many disks, as was done here. This release is not the same contents as the MS-DOS release of the same name by Keypunch, although both feature Frogger clones.

209451.overview: A compilation release in the UK of several previous games: Pole Position, Dig Dug, Mr. Do!, and Pac-Man.

209466.overview: Two games in a single package. In Seawolf II, you (and potentially a friend) move subs and shoot through a minefield to take out ships above. In Gun Fight, you and an opponent (or the computer) take on the roll of gunslingers from the old west, shooting horizontally across the screen at each other.

209467.overview:
A combo release of two games. Despite appearing separately in many collections, these games were distributed together originally. 

Starfire is reminiscent of Star Raiders/dogfight ship combat; the player turns their ship vertically and horizontally, always firing to the center of the screen.

Fire One is a submarine game, shooting torpedos from the bottom of the screen to ships, with a sonar display at the top of the screen.

209501.overview:
Atari released several compilation collections in the UK on cassette, like this one labeled "TX9043"  which contains 5 games: Typo Attack, Missile Command, Centipede, Realsports Tennis, and Star Raiders.
Each game features a loading screen by Atari Corp UK which states the copyright date of 1987. Centipede is a conversion of the Atari 5200 Centipede, featuring much better graphics and sound than the original 1982 game.
It was sold with the 'Atari 130XE Starter Pack: An Introduction to Home Computing'.

Side A: Typo Attack, Missile Command, Centipede [5200]
Side B: Star Raiders, Tennis

209503.overview: You are a hunter in the jungle after game. Your shotgun points out from the bottom of the screen, and you can rotate left or right to line up your shot in the distance (at the top of the screen). Various animals of different speeds reward different point values, and you end the match by either running out of time or being shot by pygmy enemies.

209655.overview: Compilation from English Software including Jet Boot Jack, Dan Strikes Back, Hyperblast!, Captain Sticky's Gold and Firefleet.

209656.overview: Atari Smash Hits Volume 2 is a compilation that includes Jet Boot Jack, Stranded, Diamonds, Adventures of Robin Hood and Citadel Warrior. Jet Boot Jack is a repeat from the previous collection, and Stranded is the sole adventure on the disk, the rest are arcade style games.

210599.overview: Knock down aces with the yellow ball which is moved around by hitting it with your joystick controlled blue ball - although often you'll have to dodge cones. To complete a screen first eliminate the clubs (which if left will turn into roadhogs) and then eliminate the Ace of Hearts.

210837.overview:
ADAM IS ME is a puzzle video game for 8bit Atari XE/XL computers. The game is heavily inspired by the award-winning "Baba Is You" by Arvi Teikari and "Robbo" by Janusz Pelc, but with original puzzles, levels and game mechanics. In the game you interact with physical objects and words that when connected set a new game rules. 

Earth scientists have created ADAM. A modern robot with implemented AI. They have sent it into deep space, so it could find cure for Virus that had appeared on Earth out of nowhere, and gradually began to decimate the population of our planet. ADAM's task is to collect vials of samples from nearby planets, in system far away from home. Gathered materials and data, could help science, and scientists believe that its discoveries will finally reveal a drug, that will save humanity.

It turned out, that in this system, one of the stars collapsed, and this event had created a black hole. This object slowly sucks matter from another neighboring star and from nearby planets. In threatened system, which stood on the brink of destruction, various anomalies began to appear and the laws of physics known so far ceased to work correctly... ADAM has to change these laws accordingly, and find a way through all 8 planets. 

The game has source code published on Github along with a playfield editor (in Windows) to create new levels.

210933.overview: The Adventurer is a game released as a type in for the German magazine Computronic, November/December 1987. It is a multi-screen platform game in which you navigate ladders and platforms to pick up scoring squares. There are ropes dangling from the ceiling which can be used to jump over gaps - press the button to jump on, but then when on the rope, use the stick to pull down and drop off.

210936.overview:
Originally published in the German magazine "Homecomputer" December/January 1986. 

Gameplay consists of navigating a grid maze of 121 rooms to find 5 hidden items. The player opens items in a room by walking up to them and pushing into them with the joystick. However many items will be occupied by a bomb, killing the player.

211021.overview:
From Compute! April 1983, a Missile Defense type game.

The object of the game of "Air Defense" is to defend your land (at the bottom of the screen) from falling bombs. The bombs appear at various places at the top of the screen. As they fall, the player must line up the crosshair of his gunsight and fire when the bomb and crosshair are aligned. Press SPACE to fire. 

The player gets only one shot, and timing is critical. After 20 bombs have appeared, the game ends, and the player is given a score showing hits and misses and a point score. 

One of the unique features of the game is the increasing difficulty factor: as the player improves his skill, the crosshair is gradually moved toward the top of the screen, and quicker reflexes and improved technique are required to destroy the falling bombs. As a reward for increasing skill, the player earns higher point values for successive hits. In addition, the player receives a higher score the sooner the falling bomb is destroyed.

211023.overview:
From A.N.A.L.O.G. magazine January 1986.

Once your options are set (or left alone, if you like the default settings) you may press START to play. You'll then see a vertical air hockey board with the scores displayed at the top, along with the score necessary to win the game. The puck will appear in front of the serving player's paddle. That player must hit the puck to start the game. 

The game is something like Pong, with forward motion as well as side-to-side. Players control the paddles by moving the joystick in the direction they wish to move. The buttons do nothing. A score is made when the puck goes into the yellow goal area of a player, and the other player becomes the server. 

If the puck gets stuck between players, as it can in real air hockey, you may re-serve by pressing the SPACE BAR. Also, while in the play mode, you may press the ESCape key to exit the program. Finally, if you want to restart the game, press START anytime during the game (except during the goal sequence), and you'll be returned to the options screen. 

When the game is over, there's a long cheering sequence with whistling fans (if the crowd likes you) before you're returned to the title screen.

211026.overview:
"Albert" is a PAL-only game released both in a free and commercial version (the commercial version has an additional 10 levels). It features fairly simple platform gameplay; the character Albert runs about gathering gemstones while avoiding insects. 

While the gameplay is fairly standard, the graphics are exceptional and look more like a 16-bit game instead of over 40-year-old 8bit hardware. The screens are very colorful and detailed, sprites are large, and scrolling smooth as you play through.

211034.overview:
Alien Blast is one of the few Atari 8-bit games released that was not from Atari itself but supports the Atari light gun (included with the XEGS system, but rare elsewhere). 

It is a simple Space Invaders type game, except the gun is used to aim and shoot. It appears the code attempts to compensate for the offset of the "sights" of the gun from the barrel, but generally this just comes across as inaccurate positioning when shooting.

211037.overview: The game is a tank battle simulation similar to Battlezone. The player maneuvers the tank with the stick, avoiding obstacles and shooting enemies in a 3-D playfield.

211105.overview: Adalmar is a German language single player war strategy game for the Atari 8-bit line of computers. It was a joint development project from Condor Soft and Futurevision, and published in 1994.

211592.overview:
The Amulet is a text adventure game with the usual noun/verb parser, although adjectives and conjunctions can also be used, e.g. "PUT BENT NAIL IN SMALL FIRE". It was released both commercially and as a magazine disk feature.

The game included a setup story, reproduced below.

THE LEGEND OF THE CIRCLE OF NINE 
(which you need to read to understand the adventure) 

Many years ago, in the area we now call 'The Desolate Lands' there dwelt a nation born of wizards and witches. There was strong magic in those days and those who could manipulate the magic became powerful leaders, each with a following at loyal supporters. Throughout 'The Bitter Years' many fierce battles were fought between the opposing followers of the warlocks and witches, often resulting in tragic loss of human life, but seldom realty affecting the leaders themselves. This all changed with the arrival of Gadora. Some say she was the devil herself, others have darker thoughts, but most agree that it was Gadora who brought about the formation of 'The Circle of Nine'. Her strategy of war was simple: Her spells were cast to weaken the wizards and witches, then her soldiers rode in and killed them. The people conceded. Some of the finest areas fell under her command and her army pillaged and raped the population.

Nearly a third of the known world fell to her. before the remaining nine leaders realised that they must pin forces if she was to be defeated. A pact was entered, a demon summoned and 'The Circle of Nine' was founded. The combined powers of the circle members prevailed and Gadora was denied her desire to conquer. Such was her strength however, that even the might of the Circle could not destroy her entirely, she was stripped of her powers and exiled forever from the known world. Then began the era that was to be remembered as 'The Golden Years'. an age of unprecedented enlightenment. The wizards and witches still ruled the land but instead of using their magic against each other, they joined tomes and created new spells. Spells that brought water to the arid deserts, a new hardier grain to the fields and cattle that grazed contented in the new green pastures The people grew strong in the shade of the Circle's protection and they crafted in leather and wood, bronze and iron and brewed fine wines As news of the Circle of Nine' and their spells spread, so more and more travelers came to view these events for themselves. Many brought their families and many settled and the community flourished and prospered. The members of the Circle rejoiced in the knowledge that they were well loved by the people of the land and from time to time certain special spells would be cast for the peoples entertainment and enjoyment. In return. the people continued to provide food, wine and clothing for the Circle members, as their fathers and forefathers had done.

211607.overview: Ardeny 1944 is a Polish language two-player tactical turn-based strategy game with elements of strategy board games, similar to the Panzer General series. The game is set during the World War II. The players take command of Allied and German forces during the Ardennes Offensive in December 1944. The game is divided into turns, such as construction of fortifications, replenishment of troops, movement of troops, attack on enemy units.

211984.overview: A compilation volume that includes the following games: Jet Boot Jack, Airstrike 2, Batty Builders, Breath of the Dragon, and Neptune's Daughters. All except for Breath of the Dragon had been released previously to this collection.

211985.overview: A compilation of previously released titles: Elektra Glide (also on the previous "Smash Hits"), Drelbs, Timeslip, and Fort Apocalypse.

212022.overview: A compilation of previously released games: Chop Suey, Fire Chief, Kissin' Kousins, and Hijack.

212023.overview: A compilation of previously released titles: Chop Suey (also on the previous "Smash Hits"), Quasimodo, Mediator, and Elektra Glide.

212024.overview: A compilation of previously released titles: Alley Cat, Colossus Chess 3.0, Elektra Glide, and Blue Max.

212125.overview: Atlantis Ultimo Uomo (Last Atlantis Man) is a basic shooter, where the player controls fixed gun platforms at the bottom of the screen and shoots enemies crossing horizontally towards the top. It is similar to the earlier "Atlantis" from Imagic (both set in Atlantis, both shooters, both fixed gun platforms) but is a different game.

212126.overview:
Atomic Gnom is a Shamus clone, as in that game the player character walks through a maze with electrified walls that can kill on touch, throwing knives to take out opponents in each room, and collecting items needed to progress.

Originally released by Zong in 1989, but was later re-released in 1995 by Powersoft.

212173.overview:
Airline is a business strategy game for 1 - 4 players.

Game play allows for 1 - 4 human or computer opponents. The winning goal is to maximize funds during a play session, with a pre-specified turns of turns. The game is played on board in a 6 x 6 grid, with each section representing a major US city. During each round, a player can either purchase an airport, a plane, or skip the turn. Different locations and planes are worth different profit margins. Once two or more airports are purchased, the player can station planes in different locations. Planes available in increasing cost are: Prop, Airbus, DC-10, 747, and Concord. The player will then gather fares from their connecting flights, allowing them to further expand their aviation network. 

The 1986 German game from Ariolasoft is essentially the same game, but an enhanced version released four years after this, although only in Germany.

212209.overview: Action Classics Volume 1 is a combination of two previously released games: Pitfall! and Demon Attack. Both are ports of 2600 titles of the same name to the 8-bit computers, with an emphasis on accuracy of reproduction.

212312.overview:
In avoid you control a player ship at either the bottom or top of the screen (bottom is player one, top is player 2). Player level is selected before start and a "0" means no player for that position.

The object is to score enough points by shooting up (or down) the screen at your opponent or other spaceships. Your ship can move side to side by not vertically; going all the way either screen edge is a "crash" and after 5 crashes your game is over. You also only get one shot for each change of direction, although there is no limit to number of shots if you keep changing direction.

213151.overview:
Anthill is a 2-player maze navigation game for the 8-bit Atari computer.

Two players, represented by a blue and green square attempt to navigate a rapidly changing maze to go from the bottom of the screen to the top. The first player to reach the top is the victor. If a maze piece appears on top of the player, they are sent back to the start of the maze.

213531.overview: Benny has gone out for a day in the Country. He is tastefully dressed in his favourite pair of Pink Striped Bermuda Shorts. Unfortunately there is a particularly Vicious colony of ants in the field where he is taking a Picnic and the sight of Benny's Shorts drives them Mad. The only way Benny can stop them is to stamp on them before they can reach the centre where they will stand on each other until they can invade Benny's Bermudas. Unfortunately the more ants Benny squashes, the madder they get and the faster they run. The red ants are the most difficult to kill.

214349.overview: Alien Attack is a crosshair shooter for the Atari 8-Bi line of computers. It was developed by Andrew Guillaume for Visionaire Software and published in issue 75 of New Atari User dated January / February 1996 (bonus game on magazine disk).

215193.overview: Bundesligatabellen is a football (soccer) management game. It does not have a simulated play, but instead you are intended to use it as a tracker of sorts by entering results from real matches.

215289.overview: Agent 009 is a text adventure for the Atari 8-bit line of computers. It was heavily inspired by Ian Fleming's classic James Bond novels. The game was developed and published by Jeff 'n Jeff in 1984.

215291.overview:
Atlas of Canada is a program for learning the provinces of Canada, their capitals, and various landmarks. The landmarks include lakes, islands, bays, rivers, straits, and prominent cities. The program draws an outline of Canada, and then highlights a province and its capital, or landmark. You identify the entity based on its position on the map, and a clue (for example "province" or "river"). If you guess wrong, the correct name displays. The outline then changes to blue and the program repeats these steps for another entity until all the provinces and their capitals, along with the landmarks, are outlined on the map.

Atlas of Canada displays your number of correct answers as you prgress through the game. It presents the provinces and landmarks in a different order each time you begin a new session.

The game was coded in Atari BASIC by Ronald Borta, and published by APX in 1982.

216140.overview:
Arachnid is a 1-player arcade game for the 8-bit Atari published in SoftSide Magazine 04/83.

The player controls a highly-technical robotic spider clone, which the player must try to keep alive on a plexiglass viewing area filled with radioactive alien spiders. In order to stay alive, the player must eat fruit and other spiders that are colored brown or red, while avoiding blue and yellow colored items. Some of these items fluctuate in color. The player gains health when they eat the correct colored food, but lose health when moving, or eating the wrong colored food.

Every 1000 points, the player progresses to a more difficult level, with 10 levels in total. There are 3-speed options. On higher levels, the player must avoid the green Flying Zapper, which instantly destroys the player. The highest levels contain 2 or 3 Zappers.

216218.overview:
Published as a type-in game in Page 6 Magazine, Amazing! is an arcade puzzler where your goal is to help Excephorous II to prolong his life and succeed in his quest by collectingdiamonds and avoiding those pesky lightningn bolts.

All you have to do is move our little friend from the bottom right of the screen to the top left, but the further you go the harder It will be to avoid those bolts of lightning. Those lightning bolts use up the oxygen in the underground caverns so you only have a certain amount of time to find the exit and a rising warning alarm only adds to the tension. It can get rather fraught at times.

217648.overview:
Multi-themed educational game centered around famous Peruvian food brand D'Onofrio.

Four games included: Mathematics, Civics, Geography and Physics.

418948.overview:
Alien Adventure is the second in a series of monthly text adventures for multiple systems.

Based upon the movie Alien, you are the sole survivor of the Nostromo, on a mission to deliver a cargo of oil to the Earth. A crash landing has left you stranded on an alien planet, and you must gather supplies to enable you to return to the Earth aboard your escape shuttle. During the player's adventure, they must avoid the aforementioned alien, while looking for artifacts and supplies hidden through the alien planet and a crashed alien vessel that is remarkably similar to that seen in the original movie. These include oxygen, a map to the Earth, an alien teleporter, fuel, a diamond, an alien gem, and more. The difficulty level determines how many turns available until the alien arrives and kills the player.

All commands are via 2-word VERB NOUN entries, and game play contains several object puzzles. There is no save or restore feature.

418949.overview:
Arabian Adventure is the first in a series of monthly text adventures for multiple systems.

Princes Jasmine has been kidnapped by the evil wizard Rex. He has taken her to his castle, where she is imprisoned. You must find the wizard's castle, and destroy him, to rescue the princess.

During the player's adventure, the must seek help from a genie, explore hidden caves, and travel across the sea. Enemies including skeletons, cyclops, and sea monsters block the player's path. Ultimately, the player finds the princess in miniaturized form, and must be brought back to her home, where a potion must be created to return her to normal size.

All commands are via 2-word VERB NOUN entries, and game play contains several object puzzles. There is no save or restore feature. Various monsters are found at specific locations, which can be defeated in text-based combat. Combat consists of attacking the enemy, but there are no hit points.

418952.overview:
Around the World in Eighty Days Adventure is the sixth in a series of monthly text adventures for multiple systems.

The player tries to complete the feat of recently successful Phileas Fogg, by also traveling around the world in eighty days using available technologies of the time. The player starts in London, and takes a hot air balloon ride to Barcelona, Spain. From there, they explore the desert, and take a yacht to Marseilles, France. In Marseilles, the player must outsmart punks, and take the train to Italy. In Italy, the player must scare a fat woman with a mouse to take a steamship to Bombay, India. While attempting to take a train across India, the player becomes stuck in the jungle, and must befriend some elephants to travel across the subcontinent. While traversing the jungle, the player rescues an Indian princess, and arrives in Ahmadabad, India, and then takes a train to Calcutta. The player just barely makes a steamship to San Francisco, and travels across North America, getting some help from Tinkerbell along the way. The player ultimately arrives in London with one day to spare.

All commands are via 2-word VERB NOUN entries, and game play contains several object puzzles. There is no save or restore feature.

418972.overview:
Arrow One is the thirteenth in series of monthly text adventures for multiple systems.

It's been 3 years now, 3 years since your mission into deep space. Your name is Adam Trent, explorer, trouble-shooter, and all around good guy for the Federation of Space. Your journey aboard Arrow One has come to an end: an uncharted planet the council asked you to explore. Slowly you descend onto this strange new world.

All commands are via 2-word VERB NOUN entries, and game play contains several object puzzles. There is no save and restore feature.

418979.overview:
Alaskan Adventure is the nineteenth a series of monthly text adventures for multiple systems.

You're in Alaska, standing in the snow. Around you, fifteen treasures are hidden. Some are buried in the snow, others are cached in nearby igloos. Some are in even stranger places, and you will need considerable ingenuity to get them. The player must travel to 8 separate frozen areas via dogsled. The player's goal is to return all the items to the trading post, and many of the items are found in local snow drifts or stolen from the nearby Inuit community. Along the way, the player's dogsled team will often break down, requiring the player to feed them, get them water, or treat their illness to continue to the next area.

All commands are via 2-word VERB NOUN entries, and game play contains several object puzzles. There is no save and restore feature.

418982.overview:
A single patrol ship faces countless invading aliens, dropping relentlessly from the top of the screen. The pilot maneuvers desperately over jagged terrain between blasts from alien ships, trying to stop as many as possible from landing. How will it end? The same way most computer simulations of lone heroism against countless invaders: not well for the pilot, but perhaps a high score for the player.

Moon Patrol joined the countless clones of the coin-operated arcade games invading home computers in the 1980's. There are no astronauts to protect, just invading saucers to shoot, but the aliens keep shooting back even after they land on the hardest difficulty. Consequently, the terrain becomes a real hazard as you drop low to blast saucers on the ground. Fuel is a limiting factor, even though there is always enough to get you to the next landing pad. The problem is that you only have one pass at the pad; there is no reverse, and while you can slow down, there is no stopping. Four levels of difficulty from alien ships that do not shoot back to aliens shooting at you when coming down and after landing.

419097.overview:
Adventure Pak is a set of four BASIC games: 

1) Quest for Gold
2) Moon Survival
3) Volcano
4) Super Sleuth

419125.overview: While cleaning a closet at the Marine Biological Institute in Sandramar, France, Boris Larunge stumbled upon a document which he immediately forwarded to the scholar Janusz Perheszhöe in Chablis. Perheszhöe studied it carefully and realized it could be the most sensational discovery since the the beginning of the gold rush in California. He sat down with Captain Eugen Mone, expert diver Franz Gurgelhaß and the Spanish Consul General in Istopol. The latter, Jose Atapualga de Minelao Estrabaldi-Vacante, made the necessary preparations for an expedition under the secret name "Lemuria." A few months later, a ship was found adrift near the Canary Islands - undoubtedly the expedition's ship. Whatever you may think of it, the story seems credible. Now go and dive for the treasure. Atlantis is waiting!

419126.overview: The player attempts to solve a famous quote by solving synonyms. The player has 4 words on the top of the screen with a number of blank spaces. The player must guess the synonyms for the 4 words. For every synonym correctly guessed, all letters of that word as displayed throughout the puzzle. As the player solves synonyms, letters of the famous quote are displayed. A player completes a puzzle by solving the quote.

419127.overview: The magic of microelectronics now makes it possible for you to have a planetarium-style model of the universe in your own home. All you do is push a few buttons on your ATARI XL or XE Computer and your requested view of the universe is neatly displayed in bright, easy-to-read colors on screen. The computer handles the awesome computations and enormous amounts of data. You need only sit back and tour deep space.

419128.overview:
A logic\puzzle game of 80 levels created by Boleslav Buzek and released by Blackfire! Software in 1993. Your task in this game is to assemble molecules from atoms. The shape and composition of the molecule will be displayed in the lower left frame, the name of the molecule in the upper part of the screen. It looks easy, but there's a catch. Atoms are unstable, as soon as you set them in motion, they will stop unless there is an obstacle or some other atom. You have to combine a lot here. In the beginning, before you come up with your different combinations, you will think that you will never make it to the end of the game. However, after a while you will find out that it is real. It depends only on you.
You will be given a certain time limit to compose the molecule. If you do not manage to fold the molecule within this limit and if you do not have a sufficient number of points, from which penalty points will be deducted, the game will be over. If you have enough points, a dialog message will appear on the screen. Pressing Y will continue the game. Press the 'N key to exit the game.

After beating each level, a password will appear on the next screen. Always write this password down. It allows you to always start the game from the level from which you choose a password and write it down at the beginning of the game (you don't press the 'START' key but the 'SELECT' key).
After beating the 80th level, write down the 12-digit code that appears on the screen. If you want to place well in our contest where whoever sends us a ticket with a code and has the highest number of points (encoded) wins, practice all the levels and then project the whole game (1-80 levels) at once.

419129.overview: ALIENCOUNTER (counting) one flying saucer ... one number in the sky ... aliens landing on Earth ... is this another perfect encounter? ... celebrate with fireworks! FACE FLASH (counting, visual memory, and base ten) ready, set, go .. now you see them ... quickly count them . they disappear ... how many were there?

419130.overview:
This is a compilation of three Scott Adams adventures. It contains:

Mystery Fun House
Pyramid of Doom
Ghost Town

419131.overview: One of a series of education games developed by Educational Information Systems, and published by DLM.

419132.overview:
This is a compilation of the final three Scott Adams adventures. It contains:

Savage Island Part One
Savage Island Part Two
Golden Voyage

419226.overview:
Draw Poker is standard poker in the context of common U.S. card games where each player is dealt a five card hand and then can decide if they would like to place a bet on the first round or check (pass). The player in the game is against four other players all controlled by the computer with the names of Lucky, Shifty, Ace and Slim.

Players will be dealt five cards from a shuffled deck. All players ante $5 to the pot. Starting as in many poker games the first round requires that to open you must have a pair of Jack’s or higher to start the betting. Then each player in betting rounds hopes to build a better hand by replacing or "drawing" cards as needed. Each player begins the game with $2,000 dollars.

419228.overview:
As the name suggests, this game brings to the personal computer one of the earliest concepts to appear on arcade and dedicated console game screens: a tank duel. Players look down on a battlefield of two-dimensional obstacles and maneuver their tanks to shoot and destroy each other. Each tank has nine points of armor, allowing eight hits before the final shot destroys the tank and hands victory to the opposing player.

The tanks start each game in heavy bunkers, so the first challenge is to move out safely away from the enemy line-of-fire. Plentiful obstacles and the tanks' moderate speed means play is as much a tactical challenge as one for the reflexes. Speed on the trigger can be very important, though, because when hit a tank is relocated randomly and any shell in mid-flight disappears. In a face-off this means whichever shell lands first wins. The trigger finger must be tempered, however, as each tank can only have one shot on the screen at a time. Over-anticipating your opponent can lead to reloading at the most inopportune moment.

Different platforms provide very different play, from keyboard to joystick, color to black-and-white, as well as battlefield variations. On TRS-80's, the battlefield is fixed from game to game and obstacles cannot be destroyed. In all cases, a solitaire version is provided, putting the computer in control of one of the tanks. Its reflexes are very quick.

420109.overview: A German language text based strategy/puzzle game in which the goal is to hack a computer. The game was developed by Raindorf Soft and published by AMC-Verlag in 1990.

453821.overview:
Ambulance is a 1-player arcade game for the 8-bit Atari.

The player is the driver of a military ambulance who must rescue the battalion's wounded amidst the fighting. The player must avoid exploding bombs, and spikes set out by the enemy that will puncture the player's tires. The ambulance is equipped with three bombs to defend itself, as the player tries to pick up wounded and return them to the hospital. The player receives 100 points for each man rescued, and receives an extra life at 1,500 and 3,000 points. The player starts with three lives, and it's game over when all are lost.

454431.overview:
Arena Psychotica is a snake variant. You drive a small race car and pick up the prizes scattered around the arena by running over them. Each time you pick up a prize, your car's speed increases. Meanwhile, a monster moves about the arena at random, leaving a deadly, checkered trail. If you touch the monster, his trail, or your own trail with your car, you lose a life. 

The game also features an energizer. If you hit it, you'll turn briefly into a Gobbler. While you're in this powerful form, you can eat your way through the monster's trail, as well as your own. You receive one point for each piece of trail that you ingest.
